kafkaReserved.auto.commit.enable: it does nothing on the consumer smeltr runs, and smeltr keeps auto-commit off
kafkaReserved.client.rack: each worker sets it from its zone
kafkaReserved.compression.codec: another name for compression.type, which is set from this destination's `compression` field
kafkaReserved.enable.auto.commit: smeltr commits only once a batch is delivered, and auto-commit would mark rows done before they are
kafkaReserved.enable.idempotence: smeltr keeps it off, because an idempotent producer allows too few requests in flight for a distant broker
kafkaReserved.group.instance.id: each worker sets it from its own id
kafkaReserved.max.poll.interval.ms: fixed at 5 minutes, which caps each destination's `stallAfterSecs` field, so a slow destination cannot rebalance the group
kafkaReserved.metadata.broker.list: another name for bootstrap.servers, which is set from the `brokers` field
kafkaReserved.partition.assignment.strategy: smeltr uses cooperative rebalancing, and one member on another strategy breaks the group for every worker
kafkaReserved.queue.buffering.max.messages: set to its maximum, so this destination's `bufferBytes` field bounds the queue
kafkaReserved.receive.message.max.bytes: raised with the fetch size, which is set from this source's `fetchBytes` field
kafkaReserved.request.required.acks: another name for acks, which is set from this destination's `acks` field
kafkaReserved.sasl.kerberos.kinit.cmd: it runs a shell command on every worker, and a config may not carry one
kafkaReserved.statistics.interval.ms: smeltr needs it on to report destination throttling and buffer size
kafkaReserved.transactional.id: smeltr never begins a transaction, and a transactional producer refuses records sent outside one

commits.subject: Rotate the Elasticsearch ingest key to v2
commits.body: Quarterly rotation. Every Elasticsearch destination in both groups moves to v2; v1 stays stored until the fleet reports it running.
commits.author: Demo User

commits.subject: Send PAN-OS to Splunk trimmed, and archive it whole in S3
commits.body: Splunk gets each TRAFFIC line with only the 20 columns the SOC searches, and no allowed DNS lookups. Every line also goes to the S3 archive as it arrived, so nothing is lost.
commits.author: Priya Raman

commits.subject: Alert on storefront 5xx responses
commits.body: Server errors from the storefront also go to alerts.security, so the on-call sees an upstream outage before customers report it.
commits.author: Marcus Webb

commits.subject: Onboard storefront, bastion and CloudTrail logs
commits.body: nginx access logs to logs-web; sshd and sudo from the bastions and every CloudTrail event to logs-security. Failed CloudTrail calls also go to the alerts topic. Elastic Agent and Sentinel go to the S3 archive as they arrive, until their pipelines are written.
commits.author: Marcus Webb

commits.subject: Onboard PAN-OS and FortiGate firewalls
commits.body: Both firewall fleets normalized to ECS and indexed in logs-network. Sessions are enriched with the site from the address plan, the user's department from the HR directory, and App-ID risk. PAN-OS threats, Versa, NETSCOUT and router SNMP go to the S3 archive as they arrive, until their pipelines are written.
commits.author: Priya Raman

commits.subject: Add the Applications & cloud worker group
commits.body: Firewall collectors stay in Network security. The storefront, bastion and CloudTrail collectors get a group of their own, so each fleet deploys and scales on its own.
commits.author: Demo User
